blocking.fix: In src/metadata.rs::Object::validate_schedule_details replace the lexical zero check with an exact decimal-value zero test after schema validation. Reuse exact::Decimal (e.g. normalize its parsed Number/String text), or inspect validated mantissa digits without binary64 conversion; do not round a tiny positive decimal to zero. Determining §5.2 text: “exact-permutation only (ε = 0 everywhere, transitively)”; §4.4: “Oracles and permutation actions require ε = 0 for every gate”; §11 exposes epsilon through bennett_sched_request_set_accuracy(..., const char* epsilon_decimal). These prescribe numeric zero, not the single string spelling "0". Add tests in tests/metadata.rs and tests/cli_xam.rs using that exact record: 0, "0", "0.0" and "0.000" must parse/check/hash successfully with the pins above; "0.1" and "0." followed by 399 zeros and "1" must still reject as nonzero for the oracle. No run input or budget is needed: this is admission. JCS canonicalizes JSON numbers, not the contents of JSON strings; neither the spec nor SPEC-QUESTIONS imposes shortest spelling on decimal strings. Therefore rejecting "0.0" cannot be justified as canonicalization, and no new narrowing reading should be added.

summary:
Reviewed snapshot fd9fd84196791d86f41957dc753c2cc550c4ea0c against the accepted 0.8 clauses and the e3ae1af diff. R14-B01 and R14-B02 are resolved; verdict is revise because the requested table-level audit found R15-B01 and the surrounding admission reread found R15-B02. Neither is a demonstrated new full-parser regression: the old translation-frame length rejection remains, and the lexical epsilon test predates this diff.

Table audit: checked scalar String/Text/NAME/hash/HEX/integer/seed/decimal/endpoint/number/null/version productions; all five signature alternatives and memory slots; symbols/imports/devices/layout/data projections; schedule bindings, four-component budgets, selectors, paths and payloads; all five claim kinds and three structural rules; expected-program/table/oracle alternatives; domain bundles/cells; recursive expressions; frame slots/count maps/live ranges; certificate versions/bindings/producer/regions/verification/error/composition; and coverage entries. Optional fields were checked against their clauses and recorded encodings. Contextual checks still enforce model compatibility, signature equality, required selected schedule payloads, concrete allocation class, executable subjects, claim indices, expression arity/environment, domains and point bindings. The specific structural error is the translation frame’s Array in place of the explicit two-point tuple. No other field-type/optionality mismatch was established. The table-derived positive family is evidence about the implemented grammar, not an independent oracle for that grammar’s correctness.

Required method (1): hand-derived inc8(255) at B=3 as (0,0,3), at B=2 as (0,1,2), and at B=0 as (0,1,0); CLI agrees. Reconstructed byte-exact LF envelopes independently with literal signature/body text: singleton X action 160 bytes -> 2fcd5b3d60b42ba6092447586a2157bf44ba3a6479ab2eb319bb67665feab8be; inc8 261 bytes -> 8ce5e64f15830d8e596ba9b4861def6565dd567b5804300f427d8b9566d5be93. Certificate deletion independently reproduces both object pins. X sends singleton domain t=0 to tuple [1], matching the verified evidence control.

Method (2): traced inc8’s add inverse: restore old pc, cancel successor, swap r back to its old value, XOR the recomputed modular sum out of its slot; CLI reversal of two steps restores the entire entry tuple and clean frames. Also checked mixed call/ret inverse ordering against §3.7 and traced nested/f/g’s §7.4 completed-segment reversal, including clock and memory restoration and skipping already-cancelled frames. CLI nested reversal reports equals_entry and memory_equals_entry with identical d200538a…4c memory digests.

Method (3): reviewed SPEC-QUESTIONS 1–32 against their cited rules; no new contradictory reading was established. In particular entries 11, 17 and 21 explain sketch encodings, canonical integer representations and full tuples; they do not change the explicit translation-frame cardinality or make "0.0" nonzero. Entries 31–32 retain the settled dotted-path limitation and namespace reading.

Method (4): searched production Rust for todo!/unimplemented!/unwrap/expect/panic/unreachable and unsupported/TODO/simplification/assumption/approximation markers. Hits divide into test assertions, validated representation/container invariants, internal graph/history invariants, explicit unsupported-model diagnostics and approximate display routines alongside exact semantic decisions; no new panic/fallback witness was established. Staged Unverified claim outcomes remain disclosed.

Method (5): compared §4.1–4.8 instruction families, §5.4 faults, §3.6–3.7 slot/frame forms, all metadata productions and documented CLI command dispatch; no additional missing dispatch was established. Rereading focused on the schema rewrite and its reachable admission, identity, execution and reversal paths; passing tests is not a proof of every ISA behavior.

Replayed all six original R14 files with check/hash and independently hashed their bytes; positive Y control succeeds and negative Y rejects. Direct unchanged-source grammar probe accepts translation frames of lengths 0,1,2,3, while full parse rejects the malformed frame; zero-epsilon witness rejects under both CLI commands while 0 and "0" controls succeed. The five ignored sweeps were not rerun in this review; the editor’s recorded successful runs remain historical evidence.
